title: Word Ladder
description:
A transformation sequence from `beginWord` to `endWord` is a list of words `beginWord -> w1 -> w2 -> ... -> endWord` where consecutive words differ in **exactly one letter** and every word after `beginWord` belongs to `wordList`.

Return the **number of words** in the shortest such sequence (counting both ends), or `0` if no sequence exists. All words have the same length and consist of lowercase letters.

examples.explanation: cat -> cot -> cog -> dog uses 4 words. No 3-word chain exists because cat and dog differ in all three positions.
endWord is not in the list, so no sequence can end there.

constraints: All words have the same length and are lowercase
hints: Words are nodes; an edge joins two words differing in one letter. Shortest path in an unweighted graph means BFS.
Generating neighbours by comparing every pair of words is O(N^2 * L). Instead, for the current word try all L * 26 single-letter replacements and look them up in a set.
Remove a word from the set when you enqueue it so it is never visited twice. Count BFS levels starting at 1 for beginWord.
signature: def ladderLength(self, beginWord: str, endWord: str, wordList: List[str]) -> int:
approach:
**Key insight: this is single-source shortest path on an implicit unweighted graph, so BFS gives the answer, and neighbours are enumerated by mutating one letter at a time rather than by comparing word pairs.**

**Algorithm.** Put `wordList` in a set; return 0 if `endWord` is missing. BFS level by level from `beginWord` with `steps = 1`. For each popped word, if it is `endWord` return `steps`; otherwise for each position and each of the 25 other letters, form the candidate, and if it is in the set remove it and enqueue it. Increment `steps` after each level.

**Why it works.** Each level contains all words reachable in exactly `steps - 1` substitutions and not earlier, so the first time `endWord` is popped we have the shortest chain. Removing words on enqueue is the visited set and ensures O(1) work per word per neighbour attempt.

**Common mistakes:** building the adjacency by comparing all pairs (O(N^2 L), too slow for 5000 words); checking `endWord` when enqueueing but forgetting the case `beginWord` is one step away; returning the number of *edges* instead of words; not handling `endWord` absent from the list.

**Interview follow-ups:** Return all shortest sequences (Word Ladder II)? (BFS recording parents per level, then DFS backwards.) Speed it up? (bidirectional BFS, expanding the smaller frontier; or pattern buckets like `h*t` to precompute neighbours in O(N L).) Letters with different costs? (Dijkstra.) What is the branching factor and how does it bound the complexity? (L * 25 candidates per word, each O(L) to build and hash, so O(N * L^2) total.)

complexity.time: O(N * L^2) where N = len(wordList), L = word length
